messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

Source link: https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Richard-Fair-3/publication/8439350_An_integrated_digital_microfluidic_lab-on-a-chip_for_clinical_diagnosis_on_human_physiological_fluids/links/5cf92a5892851c874c519381/An-integrated-digital-microfluidic-lab-on-a-chip-for-clinical-diagnosis-on-human-physiological-fluids.pdf
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1039/b403341h

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic (Electrowetting) Colorimetric Enzyme-Kinetic Glucose Assay on Human Physiological Fluids (Serum, Plasma, Urine, Saliva)

REAGENTS USED:
  - Calibrant (100 mg dL-1 glucose standard solution, 1.5 uL droplets)
  - Glucose Reagent (6 U mL-1 glucose oxidase, 6 U mL-1 peroxidase, 6 mM 4-aminoantipyrine, 6 mM TOPS, in 0.1 M phosphate buffered saline pH 7.0, 1.5 uL droplets)
  - Plasma Sample (1.5 uL droplets)
  - Serum Sample (1.5 uL droplets)
  - Saliva Sample (spiked with glucose, 1.5 uL droplets)
  - Urine Sample (spiked with glucose, 1.5 uL droplets; subject to uric acid interference with the Trinder reaction)

STEPS:
1. Calibration run: Dispense a 1.5 uL calibrant droplet (100 mg/dL glucose standard) and a 1.5 uL glucose reagent droplet onto adjacent electrodes (electrode pitch 1.5 mm, spacer height 500 um).
2. Merge and mix the calibrant/reagent droplet by shuttling across multiple electrodes for 15 s.
3. Measure absorbance continuously for at least 30 s using the LED-photodiode setup (545 nm green LED, TSL257 photodiode) and compute RateCALIB from the slope of the absorbance-vs-time curve.
4. Plasma assay: Dispense a 1.5 uL plasma droplet and a 1.5 uL glucose reagent droplet, merge/mix for 15 s, and measure absorbance for at least 30 s to obtain RatePLASMA.
5. Serum assay: Repeat the same dispense/merge-mix/absorbance-read cycle using serum in place of plasma to obtain RateSERUM.
6. Saliva assay: Repeat the same cycle using (glucose-spiked) saliva to obtain RateSALIVA.
7. Urine assay: Repeat the same cycle using (glucose-spiked) urine to obtain RateURINE.
8. Concentration calculation: For each sample, compute CSAMPLE = (RateSAMPLE / RateCALIB) x 100 mg dL-1.
9. Reference comparison: Compare each on-chip concentration against a reference value obtained on a bench-top spectrophotometer (Gensys 20) using a conventional 100-fold dilution; note that the urine result shows a significant deviation from the reference value, attributed to interference by uric acid reacting with hydrogen peroxide in the Trinder reaction (interference that the 100-fold dilution in the reference method suppresses but the digital-microfluidic chip's 2-fold dilution does not).

INTERPRETATION: Successful glucose quantification is confirmed by close agreement between the on-chip and reference concentrations for plasma, serum, and saliva (total error 3, 8, and 3 mg dL-1 respectively), demonstrating basic feasibility of colorimetric enzyme-kinetic bioassays on real physiological samples using an electrowetting-based digital microfluidic lab-on-a-chip; the larger urine discrepancy (16 mg dL-1) highlights a matrix-specific interference (uric acid) that must be addressed (e.g., via additional sample dilution/wash) for that fluid type.

module absorbance

manifest calibrant
manifest glucose_reagent
manifest plasma_sample
manifest serum_sample
manifest saliva_sample
manifest urine_sample

instructions:

cal = dispense 15 units of calibrant
reg_c = dispense 15 units of glucose_reagent
calib_mix = mix cal with reg_c for 15s
calib_rate = detect absorbance on calib_mix for 30s
dispose calib_mix

pla = dispense 15 units of plasma_sample
reg_p = dispense 15 units of glucose_reagent
plasma_mix = mix pla with reg_p for 15s
plasma_rate = detect absorbance on plasma_mix for 30s
dispose plasma_mix

ser = dispense 15 units of serum_sample
reg_s = dispense 15 units of glucose_reagent
serum_mix = mix ser with reg_s for 15s
serum_rate = detect absorbance on serum_mix for 30s
dispose serum_mix

sal = dispense 15 units of saliva_sample
reg_sa = dispense 15 units of glucose_reagent
saliva_mix = mix sal with reg_sa for 15s
saliva_rate = detect absorbance on saliva_mix for 30s
dispose saliva_mix

uri = dispense 15 units of urine_sample
reg_u = dispense 15 units of glucose_reagent
urine_mix = mix uri with reg_u for 15s
urine_rate = detect absorbance on urine_mix for 30s

if (urine_rate >= calib_rate) {
    repeat 2 times {
        wash = dispense 20 units of glucose_reagent
        dispose wash
    }
    dispose urine_mix
} else {
    dispose urine_mix
}

identity.protocol_name: Colorimetric Enzyme-Kinetic Glucose Assay on Serum, Plasma, Urine, and Saliva via Digital Microfluidic Lab-on-a-Chip (Srinivasan, Pamula, and Fair, 2004)

source.title: Digital Microfluidic (Electrowetting) Colorimetric Enzyme-Kinetic Glucose Assay on Human Physiological Fluids (Serum, Plasma, Urine, Saliva)

ir.content:
bsbbif_2_t:
bsbbif_3_f:
	dispose(urine_mix1[0])
	jump: bsbbif_4_j
bsbbif_4_j:
	NOP
main:
	cal1[0] = dispense(calibrant)
	reg_c1[0] = dispense(glucose_reagent)
	calib_mix1[0] = mix(cal1[0], reg_c1[0]) @ 15.0SECOND
	calib_rate1[0] = detect(absorbance, calib_mix1[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	dispose(calib_mix1[0])
	pla1[0] = dispense(plasma_sample)
	reg_p1[0] = dispense(glucose_reagent)
	plasma_mix1[0] = mix(pla1[0], reg_p1[0]) @ 15.0SECOND
	plasma_rate1[0] = detect(absorbance, plasma_mix1[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	dispose(plasma_mix1[0])
	ser1[0] = dispense(serum_sample)
	reg_s1[0] = dispense(glucose_reagent)
	serum_mix1[0] = mix(ser1[0], reg_s1[0]) @ 15.0SECOND
	serum_rate1[0] = detect(absorbance, serum_mix1[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	dispose(serum_mix1[0])
	sal1[0] = dispense(saliva_sample)
	reg_sa1[0] = dispense(glucose_reagent)
	saliva_mix1[0] = mix(sal1[0], reg_sa1[0]) @ 15.0SECOND
	saliva_rate1[0] = detect(absorbance, saliva_mix1[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	dispose(saliva_mix1[0])
	uri1[0] = dispense(urine_sample)
	reg_u1[0] = dispense(glucose_reagent)
	urine_mix1[0] = mix(uri1[0], reg_u1[0]) @ 15.0SECOND
	urine_rate1[0] = detect(absorbance, urine_mix1[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	if urine_rate1[0] >= calib_rate1[0]	|	true: jump bsbbif_2_t	|	false: jump bsbbif_3_f
bsbbr_5_h:
	PHI wash1 = {wash0,wash2}
	PHI REPEAT_21 = {REPEAT_20,REPEAT_22}
	if REPEAT_21[0] > 0	|	true: jump bsbbr_6_t	|	false: jump bsbbr_7_f
bsbbr_6_t:
	wash2[0] = dispense(glucose_reagent)
	dispose(wash2[0])
	REPEAT_22[0] = REPEAT_21[0] - 1
bsbbr_7_f:
	dispose(urine_mix1[0])

numeric_mismatches.note: The paper uses 1.5 uL sample and 1.5 uL reagent droplets; BioScript has no native volume unit, so a x10 abstract-unit scaling convention is used, consistent with other translated protocols in this test set.

numeric_mismatches.field: CSAMPLE = (RateSAMPLE/RateCALIB) x 100 mg/dL not computed in-script
numeric_mismatches.note: BioScript's grammar exposes no division/arithmetic-ratio primitive between two detect variables, so only the raw calib_rate and per-sample rate values are produced on-chip; the concentration ratio itself is an off-chip post-processing step.

numeric_mismatches.field: if/else uric-acid wash branch on urine_mix
numeric_mismatches.note: This conditional dilution/wash step is an authored interpretation of the paper's discussion of urine interference, not a step the paper explicitly specifies as an automated corrective branch.

numeric_mismatches.field: integrated lab-on-a-chip architecture (Fig. 3) and pipelined dual-assay operation (Fig. 5)
numeric_mismatches.note: Not modeled. These describe the reservoir/bus/mixing-area hardware architecture and a parallel-pipelined two-assay demonstration, which are system-integration and throughput results rather than part of the core sequential calibrant + four-sample glucose assay procedure captured here.
